canonical_definition_master: Cropland gross primary productivity indicating drought-induced physiological suppression and reduced biomass production.
Trend or anomaly in near-surface air/land temperature that increases evapotranspiration demand, moisture stress, and downstream water scarcity risk.
merge_notes: Merged repeated mentions (temperature rise/LST trend) into one canonical concept; keep per-paper context in evidence layer.

canonical_definition_master: Leaf area index as a structural canopy indicator for drought stress detection and productivity decline.
Composite climatic moisture index (for example Thornthwaite-Mather) combining precipitation and PET to represent aridity-humidity conditions.
Coverage or share of watershed/rainwater-harvesting interventions that moderate runoff losses and drought impact.
Root-zone or near-surface soil moisture condition mediating meteorological stress into crop and recharge outcomes.
merge_notes: Merged repeated mentions across drought/groundwater/rainfed contexts; keep qualifier/scope in evidence records.

canonical_definition_master: Satellite-derived solar-induced fluorescence proxy for photosynthetic activity and drought-related physiological stress.
Reservoir/river/lake surface-water availability or storage condition relevant to hydrological drought propagation.
Increase in mean or seasonal temperature used as an exogenous climate stress driver in crop-response pathways.

canonical_definition_master: Vegetation greenness/health indicator (for example NDVI-based) linked to moisture and groundwater condition proxies.
Near-surface wind speed affecting evapotranspiration demand and erosion risk in dryland systems.
Geophysical electrical resistivity indicator of aquifer saturation and subsurface hydrogeological conditions.
Thickness of weathered/saturated aquifer zone indicating groundwater storage potential.
Aquifer transmissivity or related hydraulic property controlling groundwater response to recharge and extraction.
Built-up or urbanized land extent affecting infiltration, runoff partitioning, and recharge potential.

canonical_definition_master: Stream-length density indicating runoff concentration versus infiltration potential for recharge.
Groundwater storage anomaly from gravity/satellite products representing basin-scale depletion or recovery signals.
Lineament density proxy for fractures/secondary permeability controlling groundwater movement in hard-rock settings.
Groundwater nitrate concentration indicating agrochemical pressure and irrigation-linked water quality degradation.
Population density or growth pressure driving domestic/agricultural water demand, land conversion, and extraction stress.

canonical_definition_master: Terrain slope controlling runoff-infiltration partition and recharge suitability.
Soil texture/permeability class governing infiltration, percolation, and recharge behavior.
Topographic wetness index proxy for flow accumulation and wetness patterns linked to groundwater potential.
Fraction/trend of urban impervious area associated with recharge suppression and groundwater stress.

canonical_definition_master: Canal conveyance seepage losses reducing irrigation reliability and contributing to waterlogging/salinity pathways.
Crop-specific water requirement/intensity influencing irrigation demand and crop-mix shifts under scarcity.
Intensity of power subsidy for agricultural pumping influencing groundwater extraction incentives.
Energy use/cost intensity for groundwater pumping under rainfall deficit conditions.
Chemical fertilizer application intensity influencing nutrient leaching and water quality stress.

canonical_definition_master: Reliability or adequacy index of irrigation water supply relative to demand.
Adoption share of drip/sprinkler systems as a water-saving adaptation and irrigation-efficiency mechanism.

Marginal economic value/opportunity cost of irrigation water under scarcity constraints.
Efficiency of converting water use into biomass/yield or productive output under constrained water availability.

Monetized welfare or equivalent-variation loss attributable to water scarcity and related impacts.
Adoption share of crop insurance as a risk-transfer response to rainfed production uncertainty.
Fraction of crop residues burned, affecting soil health, emissions, and agro-ecological resilience.
Adoption share of drought-tolerant crop varieties as a climate risk adaptation variable.
Farmer participation in cooperatives/producer groups influencing adaptation uptake and institutional support.
Fertilizer consumption intensity or share representing input-use context in low-water systems.

Access to formal agricultural credit enabling investment in adaptation and risk management.
Adoption share of intercropping as diversification strategy reducing rainfed crop failure risk.
Operational farm size as structural context for adaptation capacity and technology uptake.
Livestock mortality/migration impacts linked to drought-driven fodder and water shortages.
Availability of non-farm income that buffers household risk and affects adaptation decisions.
Wind/water soil erosion rate reducing soil depth, fertility, and moisture-retention capacity.
Soil organic carbon stock/concentration affecting soil health, water retention, and productivity resilience.
Index-based measure of varietal diversification as ex-ante risk management in rainfed farming.
Soil water-holding capacity controlling moisture persistence between rainfall events.
